text:
ben: quick sanity check — bringing up gemma-7b-v2 after converting weights. running our 5k prompt eval and seeing ~1.8x perplexity increase vs llama-7b baseline. conversion logs looked clean but suspicious about head-dim / rotary mapping. anyone bumped into this?

marta: what conversion path did you use? hf->ggml or from the vendor ckpt? 

ben: vendor ckpt -> our conversion script (tokenmap + head-reshape). no obvious shape errors. sample diff shows same logits flow but top tokens shifted.

ciara: shifting top tokens screams token-id remap or tokenizer vocab offset. did you compare token ids for sample inputs between models?

ben: yes, for the same prompt token ids match after our vocab_map. but when running decode the token probabilities look like they correspond to neighbouring tokens (off by small index).

arvind: could also be rotary sin/cos orientation or headwise reorder. gemma uses head grouping in export sometimes. check if the head order in the checkpoint matches our runtime ordering. i.e. head-major vs head-minor layout.

marta: good point. quick check i run locally:
```python
# map heads if needed
def reorder_heads(tensor, old_layout, new_layout):
    # naive reshape/reorder helper used in conversions
    return tensor.reshape(*old_layout).transpose(new_layout).reshape(-1)
```
if that mapping is off you'll get cross-head leaks that look like token shifts.

ciara: also test flipping rotary phase sign. we've seen a sign flip produce token-level hallucination that looks like a vocab permutation. try negating rotary angles in the runtime as an experiment: rotary_phase *= -1

ben: ran two quick experiments: 1) swapped head order per your guess -> ppl dropped to baseline+5% (much better). 2) applied rotary sign flip -> tiny improvement on some prompts but not consistent.

marta: sounds like head ordering is the main culprit. do you still see the issue after running full eval? any quantization steps in the pipeline?

ben: we do int8 post-conversion quant to save memory. i tested both float32 and int8; float32 still had offset issue until head reorder fix, int8 amplified the reg a little. probably because quant buckets end up mixing heads more.

arvind: okay actionable: add an automated head-layout detector in the conversion pipeline. heuristic: compare a small probe prompt's KV cross-correlation patterns between reference and converted weights. if mismatch, try permutations (swap blockwise) and pick lowest perplexity. cheap and effective.

ciara: i've got a tiny script that does binary-search-like head swaps and reports eval score. dropping it here:
```bash
# run from repo root
python tools/head_permute_search.py --model ./converted/gemma-7b-v2 --prompts eval/prompts_small.json --out best_perm.json
```
It tests block swaps (4-head blocks) not full factorial.

ben: running that now. also filing a conversion followup: we should log original head layout in metadata and keep a mapping. saved me hours. :pray:

deploy-bot: Model upload: gemma-7b-v2 converted by ben at 2026-03-20T16:24:10Z (sha256:abc123...).

marta: nice. once ben posts best_perm.json can we re-run full eval and a quick quality regression check against our NLG suite? if that passes we'll tag for dedicated serving tests.

ben: putting results in the eval run: ppl baseline 16.2, pre-fix 29.1, post-fix 17.4. saving artifacts to run/2311223344/. i also left the head-permutation map in metadata.

ciara: cool — create a small integration test for future conversions: apply detector + run 200-shot golden prompts and require <1.1x baseline perplexity before marking conversion complete.

arvind: +1. also add a note about int8 sensitivity in the conversion README so teams remember to re-eval after quant.

ben: 👍 will PR the detector and README. thanks all.
